goal: On /crates/:id, render 'Edit crates' and '+ Add a record' (and the empty-crate 'Add a record' link) only for the viewer's own crate, or for an ownerless crate when the viewer is an admin, with tests for every case.
description:
Web client only. Make no API, schema or shared-type changes. Do not change canEditCrate. Hide controls by not rendering them (no disabled state, no CSS).

1. apps/web/src/utils/permissions.ts: leave canEditCrate exactly as it is and add a new export next to it:

export function showsCrateActions(user: PublicUser | null, crate: { ownerId: number | null } | null | undefined): boolean {
  if (!user || !crate) return false
  if (crate.ownerId === null) return user.role === 'admin'
  return crate.ownerId === user.id
}

Add a doc comment saying this is narrower than canEditCrate: an admin keeps edit rights on other users' crates but does not get the add/manage shortcuts on that crate's page. Add cases to permissions.test.ts: no user, no crate, owner, non-owner, admin on another user's crate, admin on own crate, admin on ownerless crate, non-admin on ownerless crate.

2. apps/web/src/components/LibraryToolbar.vue: change to defineProps<{ addToCrateId?: number; hideActions?: boolean }>() and change line 21 to v-if="session.signedIn && !hideActions". An absent boolean prop is false, so LibraryView's bare <LibraryToolbar /> is unaffected; do not edit LibraryView. Update the comment at lines 6-7 so it no longer implies the actions always show. The Crates/List nav stays outside the v-if.

3. apps/web/src/views/CrateView.vue: leave canEditThisCrate and the canEditCrate call in open() untouched, because spin counting must not change. Add two computeds:

const hideToolbarActions = computed(() => props.crateId !== undefined && !(library.status === 'ready' && showsCrateActions(session.user, crate.value)))
const canAddFromEmptyCrate = computed(() => props.crateId === undefined ? canEditThisCrate.value : showsCrateActions(session.user, crate.value))

Then use <LibraryToolbar :hide-actions="hideToolbarActions" :add-to-crate-id="canEditThisCrate ? crate?.id : undefined" /> and change the empty-crate link's v-if (line 149) to canAddFromEmptyCrate.

The library.status === 'ready' check is required. The library store keeps its crates array during a forced reload and after a failed one. Example: visit /crates/999, the forced reload fails, then router.push to the viewer's own /crates/1. crate.value is defined, status is 'error', and the body shows the error, so without the status check the actions would leak onto the error state. On /shelf (crateId undefined), both the toolbar and the empty-crate link keep today's behaviour. props.crateId and crate are already reactive across reused-component navigation, so do not add a key or a watcher.

4. apps/web/src/views/editControls.test.ts: in the test titled "a crate page on someone else's crate counts no spin and preselects nothing", replace the addRecord href assertion with wrapper.find('a[href^="/albums/new"]').exists() being false. Keep its title and its spin and navigation assertions. Do not add crates to this file's shared fixture, because its counts (4 tools, 8 order buttons) depend on it.

5. New file apps/web/src/views/crateActions.test.ts, with its own fixtures. Follow the visit() pattern in editControls.test.ts: createPinia, setActivePinia, session.user = user, session.loaded = true, memory router, mount a RouterView wrapper, flushPromises. Register routes library (/shelf, CrateView), crate (/crates/:id(\\d+), CrateView, props crateId: Number), list (/list, LibraryView), crates (/crates), album-new (/albums/new), album (/albums/:id(\\d+)), album-edit (/albums/:id(\\d+)/edit), profile (/u/:username), login (/login); use a Blank component for every route except library, crate and list. Stub fetch for GET /api/crates, GET /api/albums and POST /api/albums/<id>/spins (returns { spinCount: 1 }), and make the stub configurable so a test can use a never-resolving promise or a 500. Users: a non-admin (id 1, role 'user') and an admin (id 9, role 'admin'). Crate type fields: id, name, color, label, sortBy, sortOrder, albumCount, ownerId, ownerUsername, ownerDisplayName. Fixtures need a crate owned by user 1, one owned by user 2 with ownerUsername set (so OwnerLink renders), one owned by user 9, one with ownerId null, and an empty crate owned by user 2.

Cover each criterion with a test named for it:
- AC1: non-admin on another user's crate, no 'Edit crates' or '+ Add a record' text, no link with href starting /albums/new or equal to /crates.
- AC2: non-admin on own crate, 'Edit crates' href /crates and '+ Add a record' href /albums/new?crateId=<id>.
- AC3: admin on another user's crate sees neither action; on that user's empty crate there is no 'Add a record' link in the 'Nothing in here yet.' section; on a non-empty crate, clicking button.pull POSTs /api/albums/<id>/spins.
- AC4: admin on own crate and on an ownerless crate sees both, with the crateId href; non-admin on an ownerless crate sees neither.
- AC5: signed-out visitor sees neither on any crate, and the Crates and List nav links remain.
- AC6: signed-in non-admin sees neither while fetch never resolves, after a 500 load, and on 'Crate not found'. Also add the retained-store case from step 3: load succeeds, go to an unknown id, the forced reload fails, router.push to own crate, actions absent. A pending forced reload should also hide them.
- AC7: same mount, router.push from own crate to another user's crate and back, with flushPromises after each; both actions go and come back with the correct crateId.
- AC8: non-admin at /shelf with another user's crate selected (click its button.tab) and at /list still sees both actions.
- AC9: on another user's non-empty crate, '◀ Back', 'Flip ▶', 'Pull it out', the owner link and the Crates/List nav render; clicking 'Pull it out' routes to /albums/<id> with no POST for a non-admin.

Also add one /shelf assertion that an admin on another user's empty crate still sees the empty-crate 'Add a record' link, which pins the /shelf-unchanged scoping.

6. From the repo root, run npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run format:check and npm test; all must exit 0 (AC10). Single file: npm test -w apps/web -- src/views/crateActions.test.ts. Prettier: no semis, single quotes, width 100, trailing commas. Commit style: fix(web): ...

AC11 and AC12 are listed because this implementation is what they exercise. The browser tester writes and runs those checks, so do not create or edit anything under .shipyard/checks/ and do not run browser.mjs (it rewrites tracked PNGs).
